title: Partner Co-sell Pipeline Review - Cobalt Partners
summary: Quarterly co-sell pipeline review with Cobalt Partners to align on priority accounts, technical blockers, and next steps for two joint deals (Acme Corp pilot and Meridian Systems expansion). Redwood team covered Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, security artifacts (SOC 2 / KMS), and proposed a two-week pilot for Acme on Dedicated with joint benchmarks. Agreed next steps include sharing co-sell deck, security pack, and scheduling an exec intro; owners and due dates captured in action items.
action_items: Maya Chen - Share updated co-sell deck, pricing sheet, and partner playbook - 2026-11-06
Carlos Ruiz - Schedule technical deep dive + latency/cost benchmark for Acme pilot; provide benchmark template - 2026-11-10
Liam O'Connor - Send joint account list and champions for top 6 deals - 2026-11-05
Nina Patel - Draft partner MOU and pilot onboarding checklist; include SSO/SAML and KMS notes - 2026-11-12
next_steps: Exec sponsor intro (Redwood <> Cobalt) to align timeline and pricing approval
Run 2-week Dedicated pilot for Acme with defined success metrics (latency < 250ms p95, cost per 1k tokens target)
Share Redwood security pack (SOC2, ISO certs, audit logs, KMS integration guide)
Align on co-sell revenue split and referral crediting for closed deals
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45 mins | Attendees: Maya, Carlos, Nina (Redwood); Liam, Priya, Erin, Jordan (Cobalt)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're just gonna run through the co-sell pipeline and ... yeah quick status on the top deals. Carlos and Nina are with me. Liam, do you want to kick off with the high level?

[00:18] Liam: yeah thanks Maya, happy Friday. we've got six plays in flight, priority for this quarter are Acme Corp and Meridian Systems, both are high intent. Acme wants a pilot, Meridian's further along but has strong security asks.

[00:33] Priya: quick note — Acme timeline is pretty tight, they want a pilot next two weeks to show to procurement by mid-November.

[00:42] Carlos: okay that's tight but doable. for the pilot, are they expecting hosted API or dedicated? that drives the setup time.

[00:51] Erin: they asked about dedicated because they want predictable latency and isolation. procurement also asked about KMS and audit logs.

[01:04] Maya: right. we typically recommend Dedicated for pilots where customers want isolation and SLA-backed latency. Dedicated setup can be done in days if we reuse standard configs; if they want VPC peering/on-prem then that's longer.

[01:18] Jordan: also curious about pricing — partner margin / revenue split. how do we do credits or referral?

[01:26] Maya: good question. our standard co-sell is referral + discounted pilot pricing, then we negotiate revenue shares at close. I'll send the playbook with options.

[01:35] Liam: perfect. can you also share the security pack? Acme's legal is strict — SOC2 plus KMS, SAML, audit logs.

[01:43] Nina: yep we'll include our SOC 2 report, ISO cert, and KMS integration notes. note: key management for Dedicated is customer-managed KMS in most cases, we can demo that.

[01:55] Carlos: for the pilot benchmarks, we should define goals — e.g., p95 latency under 250ms for short chat flows, throughput X rps, and cost per 1k tokens target. we'll include KV cache settings and batching guidance.

[02:10] Erin: do you have examples of similar pilots? Meridian was asking for references.

[02:16] Maya: we ran a similar Dedicated pilot with Nova Partners last quarter; I'll include a short case note.

[02:24] Priya: Meridian has a long context use-case, they're using 32k token context. how does Redwood handle that with Dedicated and quantization?

[02:34] Carlos: good point. long context is supported — we recommend specific kernel selections and KV cache sizing. quantization helps reduce memory, but we should run a small benchmark because quality can shift. for enterprise rollouts we usually test quantized variants first and measure regression.

[02:50] Liam: any blockers from our side? Jordan: channel ops?

[02:55] Jordan: just around co-sell attribution — we need the reciprocal naming for closed deals. also want a single point of contact for technical escalations.

[03:06] Maya: we can do a named SE escalation path — Carlos will be the technical lead and Nina will handle onboarding and ongoing ops.

[03:15] Carlos: i'll propose a benchmarking plan — quick synthetic load and a small live sample from Acme. when's the earliest we can get credentials?

[03:24] Erin: they said they'd share a test corpus by Monday.

[03:28] Maya: great. timeline recap: Acme pilot start next Tue/Wednesday, two weeks, then results — procurement review mid-November. Meridian we'll focus on security and long-context bench; longer timeline.

[03:42] Priya: on commercials, can you outline pilot discounts vs committed Dedicated pricing?

[03:48] Maya: yes — pilot pricing typically 50% off hosted list, or we can do a time-limited Dedicated promo. for committed Dedicated we have tiered pricing and reserved capacity discounts. i'll include the two options in the deck.

[03:59] Liam: procurement may push to AWS Bedrock / OpenAI because of existing contracts. how do we position Redwood?

[04:08] Maya: highlight predictable economics, observability, and unified runtime across hosted and private deployments. also our fallback policies and rollout controls are strong for production applications. plus we have support for private deployments with customer-managed KMS when required.

[04:23] Priya: will we offer a pilot SLA?

[04:27] Nina: pilots come with operational support, but formal SLA is part of Dedicated reserved contracts. we can offer elevated response times for the pilot.

[04:36] Erin: any notes about data residency? some Meridian customers require EU data residency.

[04:41] Carlos: we can pin region routing; for strict residency we recommend Private (VPC/on-prem) control plane. that's a longer lead but supported.

[04:53] Liam: ok let's go deal by deal — Acme first. status? Priya?

[04:58] Priya: Acme is in PoC stage, champion is Sarah M., security is watching but they want to demo the latency and cost. top risk is procurement timeline.

[05:10] Carlos: for Acme i'd propose Dedicated pilot with these steps: 1) quick sandbox on Hosted to validate prompts, 2) spin up Dedicated with minimal nodes, enable KV cache and batching, 3) run latency/cost benchmarks against their sample. this should fit two-week window if credentials arrive Monday.

[05:32] Erin: do we need infra changes for their data flow? they want logs forwarded into their SIEM.

[05:38] Nina: we support log forwarding and audit logs; we'll document integration steps.

[05:44] Jordan: could the partner be the first contact for the customer in some cases? we want to own GTM motion.

[05:50] Maya: yes we'll agree on a co-sell motion per account; for Acme we can present joint at the exec intro.

[05:58] Liam: Meridian update — they've got architecture questions re: 32k context and quantization. SE deep dive requested.

[06:05] Carlos: we'll schedule a technical deep dive. i'll bring kernel/compilation folks if needed. also want to check model variant compatibility for long context — some architectures require different kernel paths.

[06:16] Priya: are there any pre-built connectors for their embedding search? they use custom vector DB.

[06:22] Carlos: we have guidance and examples for vector DB connectors; it's usually a short integration. i'll include a sample pipeline.

[06:30] Maya: any competitive intel? Liam?

[06:33] Liam: Acme is also talking to OpenAI and Anthropic; their eval sheet shows cost sensitivity.

[06:39] Maya: then we should emphasize predictable cost with caching and batching and Redwood Optimize recommendations. our Optimize toolkit can show estimated savings and suggested quantization profile.

[06:51] Erin: on security docs, what format? redacted reports or full certs?

[06:56] Nina: we'll provide redacted SOC2 and the certs; full artifacts can be provided under NDA. include KMS integration guide and SAML SSO steps.

[07:06] Jordan: about revenue split — is there a standard percentage?

[07:10] Maya: it varies; for referral deals we typically do commission-style credits, for joint-led deals we negotiate a split based on contribution. i'll include a sample structure but legal will finalize.

[07:21] Priya: action items and owners?

[07:24] Maya: yep we'll capture. Carlos will own technical deep dive and benchmarks; Nina handles security pack and onboarding; i'll send the deck and commercial options. Liam will share account contacts.

[07:36] Erin: any blockers from Redwood side for the Acme pilot start next Tue?

[07:41] Carlos: only if we don't get credentials. otherwise infra and SE time are allocated.

[07:47] Liam: i'll nudge Sarah to send test corpus Monday morning.

[07:51] Maya: perfect. anything else?

[07:54] Priya: one more — for Meridian, can we have a separate cadence for the SE deep dive next week?

[07:59] Carlos: yes i can do Wed 10am PT, i'll send an invite.

[08:05] Maya: recap: Maya send deck + pricing; Carlos schedule deep dive and benchmarks; Nina share security pack and MOU draft; Liam send joint account list and test data. owners and dates in action items.

[08:20] Liam: sounds good, thanks all.

[08:23] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and Slack channel. bye.

[44:50] End of meeting (approx).

Notes: transcript contains typical transcription noise; speaker labels sometimes overlap and words like "KV" may be transcribed as "KV cache" or "K V cache". References to product names: Dedicated, Private (VPC), Redwood Optimize, Serve runtime.
